newsitem.title: JAPAN: Recovery appearing in Japan's labour market - govt.
newsitem.headline: Recovery appearing in Japan's labour market - govt.

text.p: A recovery is appearing in Japan's labour market although overall employment conditions remain severe, the government's Management and Coordination Agency said on Friday.
"A recovery tone can be seen although the situation is still severe and we must watch future developments closely," an agency official told reporters.

The official said that the number of employed rose 1.4 percent in March to 64.89 million from a year earlier mainly due to a fall in the number of people who had lost their jobs. That number was 50,000 less than the previous year and has fallen for six months in a row.
Additional hiring by retail firms to cope with increased consumer buying ahead of the consumption tax rise on April 1 may also have pushed up the number of employed, he said.
He also pointed to a year-on-year rise in the number of employed in the manufacturing sector for the third successive month as a sign of the recovery in the labour market.
But he added that the number of unemployed, at 2.34 million in March, was still high, although an influx of new college graduates into the workforce was a seasonal factor that pushed up the total.
The official said an improvement in the unemployment rate for fiscal 1996/97 to 3.3 percent, compared with 3.4 percent for calendar 1996, was due to a rise in the number of employed.
The number of employed rose by 560,000, or 0.9 percent from a year earlier, the largest rise in five years, the official said.
